content:
Facts: Foundation sued nephew claiming deceased's 2020 holographic will appointing nephew sole heir was false, requesting nullity declaration and restitution of estate assets based on earlier 2004 will favoring foundation; nephew appeared agreeing with foundation's invalidity claims without contesting authenticity allegations or private graphological opinion concluding forgery through imitation techniques; foundation also sought damages compensation and asset return.
Legal Framework: Articles 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (holographic will formalities; nullity for form defects); Art. 115 CPC (principle of disposition; non-contestation effects); Art. 2697 Civil Code (burden of proof allocation); case law on contestation specificity requirements (Cass. 8376/2020, 4909/2022, 21227/2019).
Interpretive Issues: Whether non-contestation principle applies when defendant fails taking analytical position on plaintiff's nullity-supporting factual allegations; specificity requirements for valid challenge to authenticity claims; effect of defendant's substantial agreement with nullity request despite formal appearance; admissibility of generic restitution/damages claims lacking detailed allegations and supporting evidence; burden allocation when parties agree on invalidity outcome.
Principles Applied: Burden of analytical contestation ceases when plaintiff fails fulfilling analytical allegation burden; contribution to thema decidendum/probandum applies equally to both parties. Generic plaintiff allegation permits equally generic defendant challenge; generality relieves neither party of proof burden. Specific plaintiff allegation with lacking/generic defendant challenge exempts plaintiff from proof burden; specific allegations with specific challenge maintains plaintiff's proof burden; generic allegation regardless of challenge-specificity maintains plaintiff's proof burden. Specific challenge defined as precise unequivocal formulation impossible through question-begging or simple stylistic formulas. Strictly linked procedural structure per Art. 115 requires parties taking clear analytical position on others' factual bases; otherwise facts deemed admitted without proof need where opposing party limited itself to generically denying or questioning claim-acceptance conditions without clear specific precise refutation accompanied by suitable evidence. Uncontested facts deemed undisputed; non-contestation determines not proof-burden reversal but thema probandum reduction. Plaintiff alleged: testator bequeathed assets to foundation via 2004 will; nephew obtained 2020-will publication appointing himself sole heir revoking previous dispositions; will not from testator's hand/free will; no uncle-nephew relationship due to differences; will referenced nephew's son birth testator unaware of given contact-lack; extrajudicial analysis concluded forgery via imitation. Defendant neither contested circumstances at hearing nor preliminary brief; substantially agreed with plaintiff's nullity request. Absence of rebuttal renders alleged facts deemed proven supporting invalidity; parties agree on invalidity requiring acceptance with other issues absorbed. Restitution claim rejected as generic lacking supporting evidence; plaintiff indicated undisputed estate assets but limited itself to hypothetical reporting of alleged misappropriation using mere stylistic formulas expressed in hypothetical terms even regarding reported villa sale. Damages claim rejected; plaintiff failed preliminary allegation burden using standard clauses devoid detailed allegations; established case law permits compensating consequential damage not damage-injury itself.
